senses.def: a Christian prophet from Judea
pertaining to there being no charge or expenditure
(derivative of αἵρεσις[c] ‘division,’ 63.27) pertaining to causing divisions
pertaining to not being prevented

senses.subdomain: Precious and Semiprecious Stones and Substances
senses.def: amethyst; usually purple or violet in color (see 2.29)
the content of what is expressed in a curse
that which has been cursed
senses.comment: It is also possible to translate ἀνάθεμα in Romans 9:3 as ‘I would wish that God himself had cursed me.’

senses.def: to move up, especially of the upward movement of the sun, stars, or clouds
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand ἀνατολή in Matthew 2:2 as meaning ‘the east’ (see ἀνατολή[b], 82.1).

senses.def: east (as the direction of the rising sun)
senses.comment: In most languages east and west are related to the rising or setting sun, although in some languages there may be some local geographical feature which serves as a marker of direction, for example, the location of a particular mountain, the ocean, or a river. For north, some languages employ ‘to the left of the rising sun,’ that is to say, the direction is oriented in terms of the left hand of a person facing toward the rising sun. Similarly, south would be ‘to the right of the rising sun.’

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: dawning from on high) the bright dawn of salvation (or possibly to be understood as a title for the Messiah)
senses.comment: The expression ἀνατολὴ ἐξ ὕψους occurs in a highly poetic liturgical passage in Luke 1, and many translators have preferred to retain the more or less literal rendering. Others, however, have interpreted this as the dawning of salvation and have therefore translated ἐπισκέψεται ἡμᾶς ἀνατολὴ ἐξ ὕψους as ‘salvation will dawn upon us from heaven’ or ‘from heaven salvation will come to us as the dawn does.’ If one wishes to employ ἀνατολὴ ἐξ ὕψους as simply a title for the Messiah, one can translate ‘the Messiah will come to us,’ but it is normally better to preserve the figurative expression and relate it to the coming of the Messiah as ‘the Messiah will come to us even as the dawn does from on high.’ One may also treat the problem of interpretation in a footnote.

senses.def: pertaining to being without the Law (specifically the first five books of the OT)
senses.comment: Even from the two contexts of 1 Corinthians 9:21 and Romans 2:12, it should be clear that ἄνομος[b] and ἀνόμως carry quite different implications in different contexts. In 1 Corinthians 9:21 a phrase such as ‘without the Law’ must be understood in the sense of ‘not being under obligation to the Law’ or ‘not being bound by the Law,’ and so 1 Corinthians 9:21 must be translated in a number of languages as ‘with those who are not bound by the Law, I live as one who is not bound by the Law,’ referring in these instances to the Law of Moses. It is important, however, in rendering the expression ‘not bound by the Law’ to avoid a phrase which would mean ‘lawless’ or ‘heedless of the Law.’ In the case of Romans 2:12, the phrase ‘without the Law’ must refer to those who are ignorant of the Law and thus are not bound by it, and so Romans 2:12 must be rendered in some languages as ‘those who sin without knowing anything about the Law are lost, but quite apart from any relationship to the Law.’

senses.def: to release from control, to set free (highly generic meaning applicable to a wide variety of circumstances, including confinement, political domination, sin, sickness)
to settle or come to an agreement with regard to some dispute or issue
to cease as of a state, with a significant element of change of state involved

senses.subdomain: To Distinguish, To Evaluate, To Judge
senses.def: to judge someone or something as not being worthy or genuine and thus something to be rejected
to put or take something away from its normal location
glosses: to put out of the way
senses.comment: In Matthew 14:3 the semantic element of ‘out of the way’ is implied in the activity of ‘putting in prison.’

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἀποτίθημι[a] ‘to put away,’ 85.44) to cease doing what one is accustomed to doing
a person in the genealogy of Jesus
kind of poisonous snake; associated with lurking danger
senses.comment: The terms ἀσπίς and ἔχιδνα[a] may be used to refer to almost any kind of poisonous snake, and since at least some type of poisonous snake occurs in practically all parts of the world, there is usually little difficulty involved in finding an appropriate term. One can, however, always employ a descriptive expression, for example, ‘a snake whose bite causes death.’

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.def: of a person’s own hands
senses.comment: But in rendering Acts 27:19, it may be somewhat superfluous or even misleading to speak about throwing over the ships tackle ‘with their own hands.’ The emphasis is not upon the hands so much as the activity of the people aboard the ship. Therefore, one may better translate Acts 27:19 as ‘they themselves threw the ships tackle overboard.’ Obviously, more than the hands were employed in this activity.

senses.def: (derivative of βαπτίζω[b] ‘to baptize,’ 53.41) one who baptizes
a raised platform mounted by steps and usually furnished with a seat; used by officials to address an assembly, often on judicial matters, with a focus on judgement
senses.comment: The association of a βῆμα with judicial procedures means that there is almost always an important component of judicial function associated with this term. Therefore in translating βῆμα, it is often best to use a phrase such as ‘a place where a judge decides’ or ‘a place where decisions are made’ or ‘a judge’s seat.’ The focus upon judgment is particularly important in those passages which refer to the judgment seat of God (Romans 14:10) and of Christ (2 Corinthians 5:10).

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: a step of a foot (a distance of approximately two and a half feet or a little less than a meter)) an extremely limited or restricted space

senses.subdomain: Processes Involving the Mouth, Other Than Eating and Drinking
senses.def: the grinding or the gnashing of the teeth, whether involuntary as in the case of certain illnesses, or as an expression of an emotion such as anger or of pain and suffering
senses.comment: Though it is possible to interpret βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων as an idiom denoting suffering, it is probably better to understand this in a some what more literal sense (especially in view of biblical views current at that time concerning the next world). It may be important, however, to suggest the significance of this symbolic action, namely, ‘gnashing their teeth in suffering’ or ‘to of suffer so much as to gnash the teeth.’ As in the case of Acts 7:54, it is important to avoid an expression for ‘gnashing the teeth’ which will suggest ‘gritting the teeth’ in the sense of determination or courageous resistance.

senses.def: an adult male, with emphasis upon relatively advanced age
the young female of cattle
senses.comment: A δάμαλις ‘heifer’ would be older and bigger than a calf but younger than a cow, since ‘heifer’ refers to a cow before she has been impregnated or given birth to her first calf.

senses.def: a companion of Paul

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to be strongly irked or provoked at something or someone
a right or just verdict or judgment
pertaining to a state of being completely controlled by someone or something
senses.comment: In some languages it may be useful to render δοῦλος in the context of Romans 6:19 as a simile, ‘like slaves,’ for example, ‘for as you surrendered the parts of your body to be like slaves to obey impurity and wickedness’ or ‘… to be ordered about by impurity and wickedness.’

senses.def: one who is a slave in the sense of becoming the property of an owner (though in ancient times it was frequently possible for a slave to earn his freedom)
senses.comment: When Paul speaks of himself as a slave of Jesus Christ or of God in Romans 1:1, Galatians 1:10, and Titus 1:1, the term δοῦλος focuses attention primarily upon his belonging to Christ or to God. There are probably also important positive overtones, since in some languages of the ancient Middle East a phrase meaning ‘slave of the king’ or ‘servant of the king’ had become the title of an important person in the government. For a discussion of certain further implications of the term δοῦλος, see the discussion at 87.81.

senses.def: to insert a shoot or bud into a growing plant
senses.comment: Since grafting is not known in some cultures, it may be important to employ a descriptive phrase, for example, ‘to cause a small twig of one tree to grow in another,’ but such a descriptive phrase must almost always be accompanied by a descriptive marginal note, for example, ‘to take a bud or twig from one tree and insert it under the bark of another tree so that it will grow.’

senses.def: extension from an area or space, usually with the implication of removal out of a delimited area
a marker of cause or reason, with focus upon the source
a marker of means as constituting a source
senses.comment: Some scholars have interpreted ἐκ in Luke 16:9 as ἐκ[g] ‘apart from’ (see 89.121). This requires the reading of ἐκλίπητε (found in a few late manuscripts) for ἐκλίπω in Luke 16:9b.

senses.def: (with the genitive) a marker of instrument, with the added implication of result
a marker of manner, often with the implication of source
(with the genitive) a marker of the source of an activity or state, with the implication of something proceeding from or out of the source
a marker of dissociation in the sense of being independent from someone or something
senses.comment: In 1 Corinthians 9:19 it may be valuable to relate the first part of the verse to what immediately follows, for example, ‘for I am not a slave of anyone, but I make myself a slave to everyone’ or ‘though I am not anyone’s slave, I serve everyone.’

senses.def: a marker of the source from which someone or something is physically or psychologically derived
a marker of a part of a whole, whether consisting of countables or of mass
a marker of the aspect of cessation

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
senses.def: a marker of a point of time which is simultaneous to or overlaps with another point of time

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time with Reference to Some Point of Time: Until, Delay, Still, From
senses.def: a marker of the extent of time from a point in the past
a marker of price
a marker of the substance of which something consists or out of which it is made

senses.subdomain: High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to sit on the right side of) to be in a position of high status
glosses: to sit on the right side of
senses.comment: Compare the use of ἀριστερός in 87.35 and see the discussion of Mark 10:37 there. For another interpretation of δεξιός in Mark 10:37, see 82.8.

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: from a part) the state of being part of something
(an idiom, literally: from measure) a scalar point marking considerable limitation in the extent of some activity
senses.comment: In a number of languages this expression in John 3:34 may be appropriately rendered as ‘he doesn’t hold back at all when he gives the Spirit’ or ‘he gives the Spirit in an abundant way.’

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: from excess) an extremely high point on a scale of extent and implying excess
senses.comment: In Mark 6:51 both λίαν (78.1) and ἐκ περισσοῦ are expressions of degree and they reinforce one another.

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time with Reference to Some Point of Time: Until, Delay, Still, From
senses.def: an exceedingly long period of time from an assumed beginning up to the present
(an idiomatic frame, literally: from … to …) a degree of totality emphasizing exclusiveness or the elimination of other possibilities

senses.subdomain: High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to sit on the left side of) to be in a position of high status, but less than in the case of the right side (compare 87.34)
glosses: to be given somewhat less high status
to sit on the left side of
senses.comment: Compare the use of δεξιός in 87.34.|In a number of languages the equivalent of this entire expression in Mark 10:37 would be ‘in order that one of us may be number one and the other may be number two in your kingdom’ or ‘in order that one of us may be your first officer and the other your second officer in your kingdom.’ For another interpretation of ἀριστερός in Mark 10:37, see 82.7.

senses.subdomain: Opposite, Over Against, Across From, Offshore From
senses.def: a position over against an object or other position
pertaining to being hostile toward
to cause an object to extend in space (for example, by becoming straight, unfolded, or uncoiled)
pertaining to being oriented in the direction opposite to a movement
pertaining to being hostile toward

senses.subdomain: Opposite, Over Against, Across From, Offshore From
senses.def: a position over against an object or other position
shaking or trembling, often with the implication of fear and/or consternation
senses.comment: In a number of languages there are two distinct terms for trembling, one relating to illness (as in the case of epileptic seizures or the chills and fever associated with malaria) and the other associated with fear.

senses.def: pertaining to extreme terror or fear, often accompanied by trembling
senses.comment: In Hebrews 12:21 the meanings of ἔκφοβος (25.256) and ἔντρομος serve to reinforce each other.

senses.def: a position not contained within a particular area
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand ἔξω in Acts 16:13 as involving extension (see 84.27).

senses.def: extension to a goal which is outside a presumed area

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἔξω[a] ‘outside,’ 83.20) a person who is not a member of a particular in-group
senses.comment: See also 11.11.

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: the outside person) the physical nature or aspect of a person
senses.comment: The phrase ὁ ἔξω ἄνθρωπος is to be understood in direct contrast with ὁ ἔσω (ἄνθρωπος) in the same verse, which refers to the psychological or spiritual nature of human personality (see 26.1).

senses.subdomain: To Intend, To Purpose, To Plan
senses.def: a plan for treacherous activity against someone

senses.subdomain: To Choose, To Select, To Prefer
senses.def: to choose or select on the basis of having investigated carefully
to go to see a person on the basis of friendship and with helpful intent
senses.comment: For another interpretation of ἐπισκέπτομαι in Matthew 25:43, see 35.39.

senses.def: to care for or look after, with the implication of continuous responsibility
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand ἐπισκέπτομαι in Matthew 25:43 as meaning ‘to visit’ (see 34.50).

senses.def: to be present, with the implication of concern
glosses: to be on hand to aid

senses.def: to become not able to be moved
to be or to become encouraged and hence cheerful
senses.comment: In some languages the equivalent of ‘to become encouraged’ is ‘to have one’s heart return’ or ‘to have one’s liver stand up again’ or ‘to have one’s heart become hard again.’

senses.def: pertaining to being to the left of some point of reference
a person in the genealogy of Jesus
to lay or construct a foundation
to provide a firm basis for belief or practice
glosses: to cause to be steadfast in

senses.def: the door to a house or building (often occurring in plural form and designating double doors or gates)
the entranceway into a building or structure
senses.comment: In John 10:9 θύρα[b] is used figuratively to refer to Jesus as the means of access to salvation: ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ θύρα δἰ ἐμοῦ ἐάν τις εἰσέλθω σωθήσεται ‘I am the door; whoever comes in by me will be saved.’ In John 10:9 the emphasis is upon the door as a passageway and not as an object closing off an entrance. Literal translations of ‘I am the door’ may often lead to misinterpretation, since the term used for ‘door’ is likely to refer to a literal door rather than to the entranceway, thus suggesting that Jesus Christ functions primarily to prevent passage rather than making entrance possible.

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
senses.def: a point of time subsequent to another point of time and indicating imminence, that is to say, the subsequent event is regarded as almost begun
a marker of purpose for events and states (sometimes occurring in highly elliptical contexts)
a marker of result, though in some cases implying an underlying or indirect purpose
senses.comment: In some languages it is difficult to mark a result clause in a context such as John 9:2. This may be done, however, by restructuring the statement as ‘he was born blind; therefore, who sinned? Did this man sin or did his parents sin?’

senses.def: a marker of the content of discourse, particularly if and when purpose is implied
senses.comment: An expression of command is implicit in this passage in Ephesians 5:33, and therefore one may interpret this clause with ἵνα as being a matter of content.

senses.subdomain: Markers of Identificational and Explanatory Clauses [Epexegetical]
senses.def: a marker of identificational and explanatory clauses
the smallest letter of the Greek alphabet (corresponding to the ‘yod’ of the Hebrew alphabet)
senses.comment: See discussion in 33.37.

senses.subdomain: Events Involving Liquids and Dry Masses
senses.def: a large flood with destructive force (more intense and extensive than πλήμμυρα ‘flood,’ 14.33)
senses.comment: In the NT κατακλύζω and κατακλυσμός occur only in 2 Peter and are used exclusively of the catastrophic flood in the time of Noah. Such a flood may be spoken of as ‘a flood that destroys’ or ‘much water which destroys.’

senses.def: to do serious harm to, with the implication of misleading
a state of total ruin or destruction
to state with force and/or authority what others must do
senses.comment: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘to order’ or ‘to command’ is ‘to speak with strength’ or ‘to speak strong words’ or, in the form of direct discourse, ‘to tell others, You must …’

senses.def: a member of the church at Philippi
(derivative of κυβερνάω ‘to steer a ship, to guide,’ not occurring in the NT) the ability to lead
senses.comment: ‘The gift of leadership’ may be expressed in some languages as ‘being able to lead others’ or ‘being able to get others to follow.’

senses.def: a Roman army unit of about six thousand soldiers
senses.comment: The expression ‘twelve legions of angels’ indicates a very large group of angels; accordingly, the meaning may be rendered as ‘many, many angels’ or ‘thousands of angels.’

senses.def: the name of a host of demons
ceremonial washing referring to baptism
senses.comment: In Ephesians 5:26 the phrase τῷ λουτρῷ τοῦ ὕδατος has been generally interpreted as a reference to baptism, since the literal washing of an object by means of water would not be a means of ritual purification in the sense in which the church would be dedicated or consecrated to God. Similarly, in Titus 3:5, λουτρόν has generally been regarded as referring to baptism.

senses.def: the high priests slave whom Peter wounded
a king of Salem and priest of the Most High God in the time of Abraham
a state of defilement, involving both religious and moral aspects
senses.comment: In a number of languages, religious defilement is expressed as ‘badness in God’s sight.’ In some instances, this same concept may be expressed idiomatically as ‘ugliness of the heart.’

senses.def: a man who is about to be married or has just been married
senses.comment: In a number of languages a term for bridegroom must indicate explicitly whether the marriage is about to take place or has just taken place. Therefore, one may have to employ some such phrase as ‘a man who is going to be married soon’ or ‘a man who has just been married.’ A corresponding type of expression may be required for ‘bride’ (see 10.57).

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to show mercy and concern, with the implication of sensitivity and compassion
a cheap, sour wine (evidently a favorite beverage of poorer people and relatively effective in quenching thirst)
senses.comment: ‘Sour wine’ is sometimes rendered as ‘bitter wine’ or ‘sour juice.’

senses.def: marker of negative propositions

senses.subdomain: Markers for an Affirmative Response to Questions
senses.def: marker of an affirmative response to a question
a negative response to questions or statements or an emphatic negation of a statement
a marker of emphatic negation

senses.subdomain: Markers for an Affirmative Response to Questions
senses.def: a marker of a strongly emphatic affirmative response to a question

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
senses.def: to cause to become old and obsolete, and hence no longer valid

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
senses.def: to become old, with the implication of becoming obsolete and/or useless
senses.comment: In some languages it may be useful to translate παλαιόομαι in Hebrews 1:11 as ‘they will become old and worn out.’

senses.def: (derivative of παραμυθέομαι ‘to comfort,’ 25.153) that which causes or constitutes the basis for consolation and encouragement
to stir up hostility against
to remove something which is around something else
(a technical, nautical term) to raise the anchor in preparation for departing
to cause a state to cease
to stop doing something, with the implication of complete cessation
a source of water flowing onto the surface or into a pool somewhat below ground level
senses.comment: πηγή[a] spring differs from φρέαρ[a] and πηγή[b] well (see 7.57) in that a πηγή[a] is normally a natural source of water, in contrast with φρέαρ[a] and πηγή[b], which are dug and into which a πηγή[a] may be said to flow.

senses.def: deep constructions, often walled with stone, at the bottom of which was a pool of water
senses.comment: If there was a relatively ready flow of water, a well could very appropriately be called a πηγή[a] 'spring,' 1.78 (and this may be the reason for πηγή[a]. However, both terms are used interchangeably in certain contexts; compare, for example, πηγή in John 4:6 and φρέαρ in John 4:11, both referring to Jacob’s well at Sychar.

senses.def: (a set phrase, literally: fountain of blood) the loss of blood through menstrual bleeding
(a diminutive form of πλοῖον ‘boat, ship,’ 6.41, but in some contexts it is possible that the diminutive aspect of πλοιάριον is not relevant) small fishing boat
senses.comment: Receptor language terms to be employed for πλοιάριον, πλοῖον (6.41), and ναῦς (6.43) depend largely upon the contextual equivalents in each receptor language.

senses.def: a position at a relatively great distance, with the possible implication of comparison
a position at an even greater distance than πόρρω ‘far away’ (83.31)
(derivative of προδίδωμι ‘to betray,’ not occurring in the NT) one who delivers without justification a person into the control of someone else
to move toward a reference point, with a possible implication in certain contexts of a reciprocal relationship between the person approaching and the one who is approached
to take the initiative in association with someone
senses.comment: Though it is also true that Jews were not allowed to continue to associate with Gentiles, the focus of προσέρχομαι[b] in Acts 10:28 appears to be upon the initiative which could not be taken by a Jew in approaching a Gentile in order to be associated in some activity which would be contrary to ritual observances. προσέρχομαι in this context may therefore be rendered in some languages as 'to join arms with a Gentile,´ 'to link oneself with a Gentile,´ or 'to become a close friend of a Gentile.´

senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of προσέρχομαι[a] ‘to move toward,’ 15.77) to come to a position of holding the same opinion as someone else
glosses: to come to an opinion with

senses.def: a woman who proclaims inspired utterances on behalf of God
(an Aramaic transcription) an honorific title for a teacher of the Jewish Scriptures, implying an important personal relationship
the father of Boaz in the genealogy of Jesus
the father of Eber in the genealogy of Jesus
an event which is regarded as having some special meaning
senses.comment: In translating σημεῖον in Matthew 24:3, it may be necessary in some languages to say ‘tell us what will happen that will show that you are coming’ or ‘tell us what we will see that will make us know that you are coming.’|σημεῖον as an event with special meaning was inevitably an unusual or even miraculous type of occurrence, and in a number of contexts σημεῖον may be rendered as ‘miracle.’ Certainly that is the referent of the term σημεῖον in John 2:23 (πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦθεωροῦντες αὐτοῦ τὰ σημεῖα ἅ ἐποίει ‘many believed in him as they saw the signs he did’). For the Gospel of John, however, a σημεῖον is not simply a miraculous event but something which points to a reality with even greater significance. A strictly literal translation of σημεῖον as ‘sign’ might mean nothing more than a road sign or a sign on a building, and therefore in some languages σημεῖον in a context such as John 2:23 may be rendered as ‘a miracle with great meaning.’

senses.def: a condition resulting from the partial or complete absence of light (see 14.36)
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is impossible to speak of ‘darkness’ as being an agent in the sense of Luke 23:44 ‘darkness covered the whole country.’ Accordingly, one must say ‘throughout the whole country it was dark’ or ‘it darkened over the whole country.’ In some languages darkness may be characterized as being a quality of the night, for example, ‘it was like night.’

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: (figurative extension of meaning σκοτία[a] ‘darkness,’ 14.53) the realm of sin and evil

senses.subdomain: Not Able To Be Known, Secret
senses.def: pertaining to not being able to be known by the public but known by some in-group or by those immediately involved
a person greeted in Romans 16:9
(an idiom, literally: to bend the back) to undergo particularly difficult hardships, possibly implying forced labor
glosses: to be bent down with difficulties

senses.def: (a technical, nautical term) to be swamped with water while sailing in a boat
glosses: to have a boat filling rapidly with water

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Duration of Time: Beginning, End
senses.def: to come to the end of a period of time, with the implication of the completion of an implied purpose or plan
senses.comment: In a number of languages it may be difficult to speak of a period of time being ‘complete.’ In Luke 1:23 one may often translate as ‘when he had finished his period of service’ or even ‘when he had done his work.’ In the case of Acts 7:30, the expression ‘after forty years were completed’ may be rendered in some languages as ‘after forty years were passed’ or ‘when forty years had happened.’

senses.def: to join with others in eating elaborate meals or banquets
senses.comment: ‘To feast together’ may be expressed in some languages merely as ‘to eat a great deal together with others’ or ‘to join with others in filling one’s stomach’ or ‘to eat with others more than one should.’

senses.subdomain: Instruments Used in Marking and Writing
senses.def: an engraved object used to make a mark denoting ownership, approval, or closure of something (normally done by pressing into heated wax and usually attached to a document or letter)
senses.comment: In some languages the closest equivalent to ‘seal’ or ‘signet’ is the mark made by the seal, for example, ‘the symbol of his name’ or ‘the mark of his ownership.’ In certain contexts one may employ a phrase such as ‘the instrument by which a mark is made.’

senses.subdomain: Instruments Used in Marking and Writing
senses.def: the substance which bears the imprint of a seal or signet (see σφραγίς[a], 6.54), used for sealing a document or for showing ownership or endorsement
senses.comment: In Revelation 5:2 one may speak of ‘the wax that keeps the scroll closed,’ but in some languages it may be better to use a more general statement, for example, ‘the substance with which the scroll is sealed’ or ‘the substance that kept the scroll closed.’

senses.def: the impression of a signet ring or seal, primarily indicating ownership
senses.comment: One may also translate this clause in Revelation 9:4 as ‘who do not have the mark on their foreheads which shows that they belong to God.’

senses.def: the mark or impression made by a seal or stamp
that which confirms or attests to the genuineness of something
to give birth to a child
senses.comment: All languages have expressions for human birth, though these are frequently in idiomatic forms, for example, ‘to drop a child’ or ‘to cause a baby to pass between the legs.’ A number of languages have a variety of terms referring to giving birth, and some of these may involve unfortunate connotations. One must therefore be careful about the selection of appropriate expressions.

senses.def: an emphatic marker of result, often associated with exhortation

senses.subdomain: Pattern, Model, Example, and Corresponding Representation
senses.def: pertaining to that which serves as a model or example
to be completely and overwhelmingly victorious
a convert and friend of Paul
a place of detention
senses.comment: Practically all languages have terms for a jail or a prison, though in some instances a descriptive phrase is employed, ‘a place where people are tied up’ or ‘a place to be chained.’ In some instances, highly idiomatic expressions are used, ‘a place for eating iron’ or ‘a room with rats.’

senses.def: (derivative of φυλάσσω[a] ‘to guard closely,’ 37.120) a place or post for guarding

senses.subdomain: Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
senses.def: one of four periods of time into which the night was divided (during which time certain assigned persons would be on the lookout)
senses.comment: In general, φυλακή in the NT refers to one of four periods into which the night was divided, based on the Roman custom of dividing the night into four equal periods or watches. In Matthew 24:43 and Luke 12:38, however, it is possible that the reference is to three night watches, as was typical among Hebrews and Greeks.

senses.def: a place for wild animals and evil spirits to dwell
to be on one’s guard against some eventuality
senses.comment: In a number of languages there is a great deal of difference in terminology employed in speaking about guarding an area in order to apprehend someone and guarding a flock of animals for fear of theft from robbers or danger from wild animals.

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: an individual who pretends to be a close member of a socio-religious group but is not (see 11.22, 11.23, and 11.24)
glosses: one who only pretends to be a fellow believer in Christ
senses.comment: It is frequently necessary to make explicit the full implications of ‘false brother’ by translating ‘one who pretends to be a fellow believer in Christ but is not.’
